entries.name: Build Map
entries.description: Creates a map from the input key-value entries. For entries with duplicate keys, this function includes only the last entry in the resulting map.

terminals.name: key
terminals.description: key specifies the key of the entry. This input accepts any data type. All the keys must be unique and of the same data type.

terminals.name: value
terminals.description: value specifies the value of the entry. This input accepts any data type. All the values must be of the same data type.

terminals.name: map
terminals.description: Functions © National Instruments 1413 map returns the resulting map. Examples Refer to the following example files included with LabVIEW.

entries.name: Insert Into Map Function
entries.description: Inserts a key and its associated value into a map. If the key is already included in the map, this function replaces the original value of the key with the new associated value.

terminals.name: map in
terminals.description: map in specifies the map in which you want to insert a key-value entry. This input accepts a map of any data type. The default data type is a map of 32-bit signed integers.
terminals.default_value: data type is a map of 32-bit signed integers

terminals.name: key
terminals.description: key specifies the key of the entry to insert into the map. The key must be of the same data type as the existing keys in the map.

terminals.name: value
terminals.description: value specifies the value of the entry. This input must be of the same data type as the existing values in the map.

terminals.name: map out
terminals.description: map out returns the map with the inserted entry. Functions 1414 ni.com

terminals.name: key already included?
terminals.description: key already included? returns whether map in already includes key. If key already included? is TRUE, this function replaces the associated value of key in map in with value and returns the resulting map in map out.

terminals.name: value unchanged?
terminals.description: value unchanged? returns whether any values in the input map are updated after the insertion. Examples Refer to the following example files included with LabVIEW.

entries.name: Remove From Map Function
entries.description: Removes a key and its associated value from a map.

terminals.name: map in
terminals.description: map in specifies the map from which you want to remove an entry. This input accepts a map of any data type. The default data type is a map of 32-bit signed integers.
terminals.default_value: data type is a map of 32-bit signed integers

terminals.name: key
terminals.description: key specifies the key of the entry to remove. This input must be of the same data type as the existing keys in the map.

terminals.name: map out
terminals.description: map out returns the map with the entry of the specified key removed. Functions © National Instruments 1415

terminals.name: key not found?
terminals.description: key not found? returns whether map in includes an entry with the specified key.

terminals.name: value
terminals.description: value returns the value of the entry associated with key. Examples Refer to the following example files included with LabVIEW.

entries.name: Look In Map Function
entries.description: Checks whether a map includes an entry with the specified key and returns the associated value of the key.

terminals.name: map
terminals.description: map specifies the map in which you want to look for a key. This input accepts a map of any data type. The default data type is a map of 32-bit signed integers.
terminals.default_value: data type is a map of 32-bit signed integers

terminals.name: key
terminals.description: key specifies the key to look for in the map. The key must be of the same data type as the existing keys in the map.

terminals.name: default value
terminals.description: default value specifies the value to return in value if the specified key does not exist in the map. This input must be of the same data type as the existing values in the map. Functions 1416 ni.com
terminals.default_value: value specifies the value to return in value if the specified key does not exist in the map

terminals.name: key not found?
terminals.description: key not found? returns TRUE if map does not include an entry with the specified key. Otherwise, key not found? returns FALSE.

terminals.name: value
terminals.description: value returns the value of the entry with the associated key if key not found? is FALSE. If key not found? is TRUE, this output returns the value in default value. Examples Refer to the following example files included with LabVIEW.
terminals.default_value: value
